index.title: Administration console
index.metaDescription: The platform modules, which of them have a screen, and what the rest wait on.
index.standfirst: The {total} modules §4.11 describes. {complete} of them are finished and {partial} are partly built; each of those says what it is still waiting for, because a backlog that reads as though the console were nearly done is worse than one that names the gap.
index.footnote: No screen here is a gate. Every endpoint the console calls checks the caller itself — refusing a stranger as a stranger, and a colleague by the capability the screen wanted — and each screen renders that refusal as it arrived. A check in the browser would be a second, weaker copy of one the service already makes correctly.

AD-01.title: Project moderation
AD-01.summary: The submission queue, its three outcomes, and the decision behind each one.

AD-02.title: Trust and safety
AD-02.summary: Complaints about campaigns, and the suspension that answers the worst of them.
AD-02.waitingOn: Fraud signals and the identity review are built and scored (#108, #105), and neither has a screen here yet — both queues are reachable only through the API.

AD-03.title: Curation
AD-03.summary: Editorial collections, the badges they grant, open calls, and where they appear.

AD-04.summary: Search an account, read its standing, stop it, let it back in — and say who works here.

AD-05.title: Finance
AD-05.summary: Every charge and posting, what each creator is owed, whether it all adds up, and the signatures before it leaves.

AD-06.title: Refunds

AD-08.title: Taxonomy
AD-08.summary: Categories, subcategories and tags, with a translation per locale.

AD-09.title: Content moderation
AD-09.summary: Complaints about comments, campaign updates, and people.

AD-10.title: Support
AD-10.summary: Tickets with the account context and the history of what was done.
AD-10.waitingOn: Staff record a conversation against an account; there is no public form yet, which is a surface with its own rate limiting and anonymous-sender question (#310).

AD-11.title: Fee configuration
AD-11.summary: Platform and processing rates, their exceptions, and every set of terms ever charged.

AD-12.summary: Gradual rollout, with a kill switch that means what it says.

AD-14.title: Audit log
AD-14.summary: The immutable record of every privileged action, newest first.

AD-15.title: Email templates
AD-15.summary: Edit, preview and test send, with every version an edit has produced.

AD-16.waitingOn: Nothing here alerts. #138 is §18’s observability work and is still what will wake somebody; this page is read rather than watched (#316).

audit.metaDescription: Every privileged action the platform has recorded, newest first.
audit.title: Audit log
audit.intro: Who did what, to what, and how it came out. The table is append-only in PostgreSQL rather than by convention, so nothing on this page — and nothing in the service — can change a row that is already here.

health.metaDescription: Queue depth, failed jobs and provider status, measured when you open the page.
health.title: System health
health.intro: Measured when you open it. Nothing on this page wakes anybody, and nothing watches it while you are not looking — read it when you suspect something rather than relying on it to tell you.

flags.metaDescription: Gradual rollout and experiments, with a kill switch that means what it says.
flags.title: Feature flags
flags.intro: A rollout percentage is decided by a stable hash, so widening one only ever adds people — nobody loses a feature because the number went up. Switching a flag off overrides everything else about it.

analytics.metaDescription: Volume, success rate and average pledge across the whole platform.
analytics.title: Platform analytics
analytics.intro: Three of AD-13's five. Cohorts and funnels are not here, and the screen says what each is waiting on rather than approximating two numbers that would look like them.

curation.metaDescription: Editorial collections, what is in them, and whether the public can see them.
curation.title: Collections
curation.intro: Staff selections, themed lists and open calls — one table, because all three have a slug in a URL, translated copy, a publication decision and an edited sequence of campaigns behind them. Nothing here can be deleted: a collection anything has happened to carries the record of it, so withdrawing one takes its page down and leaves the reasoning intact.

curationSlug.metaDescription: One curated list, and the campaigns in it.
curationSlug.title: Collection
curationSlug.intro: What is in this list, and in what order. On a collection that grants the editorial badge, adding a campaign here is applying §3.2's badge to it.

curationBadges.metaDescription: Which collections badge the campaigns in them.
curationBadges.title: Editorial badges
curationBadges.intro: A campaign carries §3.2's editorial badge because it is in a collection that grants one — there is no badge table, and no way to badge a single campaign. Turning the grant on or off is therefore a decision about every campaign in the list at once.

curationOpenCalls.metaDescription: Themed programmes, and the windows they accept entries in.
curationOpenCalls.title: Open calls
curationOpenCalls.intro: A programme is a themed collection with dates. Those dates decide more than they look: the public read excludes a collection whose window has closed, so a finished programme stops answering rather than showing as finished.

curationPlacements.metaDescription: The order curated collections appear in.
curationPlacements.title: Placement
curationPlacements.intro: Where curated collections appear, which today is the order they appear in. The home page and the browse pages read the same list, so this is one decision rather than one per surface.

disputes.metaDescription: Cases a card network raised, the evidence against them, and how each ended.
disputes.title: Chargebacks
disputes.intro: Ordered by deadline, soonest first. Everything else about a dispute can be reconstructed from the provider afterwards; a deadline that has passed cannot, and losing by default is the expensive way to lose.

emailTemplates.metaDescription: The copy of every message the platform sends, and every edit anybody has made to it.
emailTemplates.title: Email templates
emailTemplates.intro: The copy that ships with the code is what the platform sends unless somebody has rewritten it. An edit appends a version rather than changing anything in place, so “what did this notice say in March” stays answerable.

emailTemplatesType.metaDescription: The shipped copy, the override if there is one, and every version anybody has written.
emailTemplatesType.intro: The subject and the first paragraph are what an administrator may rewrite. The headline, the button label and a type’s conditional second paragraph stay in the shipped catalogue — a button with no label is a broken email rather than a badly worded one.

fees.metaDescription: Platform and processing rates, their exceptions, and every set of terms the platform has charged.
fees.title: Fees
fees.intro: Changing a fee opens new terms beginning now. The closed ones stay on the screen, because “what did we charge in March” is a question §22.1 attaches a retention rule to.

plans.metaDescription: The subscription plans a creator publishes under, and the payments waiting to be recorded.
plans.title: Plans
plans.intro: A plan is edited in place, unlike a fee schedule: what a subscriber was charged is written on their own subscription, so nothing here changes anybody past bill.

ledger.metaDescription: The double-entry ledger, by account and by campaign, with both sides of every entry.
ledger.title: Ledger
ledger.intro: Every posting the platform has written, both sides shown together, newest first. The debits equal the credits on each one — PostgreSQL refuses a transaction in which they do not — and each card says so rather than asking you to take it on trust.

moderation.metaDescription: Reports waiting on platform staff, and the decisions taken on them.
moderation.title: Moderation queue
moderation.intro: Every complaint the platform has received, oldest first. Deciding a report records a judgement about the complaint and nothing else — suspending a campaign, banning an account and removing content are separate decisions with separate consequences.

moderationReportId.metaDescription: One complaint, the decision taken on it, and everything recorded against it.
moderationReportId.title: Report
moderationReportId.intro: The complaint, what was decided about it, and every privileged action recorded against it — including the ones that were refused.

moderationContent.metaDescription: Complaints about comments and campaign updates, oldest first.
moderationContent.title: Content reports
moderationContent.intro: Complaints about what somebody wrote on a campaign, oldest first. Deciding one records a judgement about the complaint — taking the comment or update down is a separate action, by somebody who can see it in context.

moderationProfiles.metaDescription: Complaints filed against a person rather than one of their campaigns.
moderationProfiles.title: Profile reports
moderationProfiles.intro: Complaints about a person rather than one of their campaigns, oldest first. Deciding one records a judgement about the complaint and nothing else — banning the account is a separate decision, taken on the accounts screen, and it signs the person out everywhere.

payments.metaDescription: Every call to a payment provider, its reference, and why the refused ones failed.
payments.title: Payment log
payments.intro: Every call the platform has made to a payment provider, newest first, including the ones that were refused. A status never moves: a pending call that later settled is a second row, so four rows for one pledge is an attempt history rather than four payments.

payouts.metaDescription: What each creator is owed, the hold it is under, and the signatures before it leaves.
payouts.title: Payouts
payouts.intro: Figures are frozen when a payout is calculated and never recomputed — the payout two people approved has to be the one that is sent. Approving needs APPROVE_PAYOUT, which the finance role deliberately does not confer.

reconciliation.metaDescription: Whether the platform’s money adds up, and what is wrong when it does not.
reconciliation.title: Reconciliation
reconciliation.intro: Three questions, each of which the other two would miss: do the debits equal the credits, does any account hold a sign it cannot, and does the ledger agree with the record of what moved. It runs nightly and reports rather than repairs — nothing here corrects anything, because the entry that would fix a discrepancy depends on which of a dozen things went wrong.

refunds.metaDescription: Full and partial refunds with reason codes, and every one the platform has issued.
refunds.title: Refunds
refunds.intro: Reading this list needs VIEW_FINANCE; issuing one needs ISSUE_REFUND. The mistakes are not comparable, which is why they are two different authorities.

staff.metaDescription: Who works here, what each role confers, and what your own account may do.
staff.title: Staff and roles
staff.intro: Roles are additive: an account holds the union of every role granted to it, and nothing here takes a capability away. Granting one is audited under your name.

support.metaDescription: Tickets with the account context they are about and the history of what was done.
support.title: Support
support.intro: Most urgent first, oldest first within a priority. There is no public form behind this yet: somebody writes in, and a member of staff records the conversation against their account.

taxonomy.metaDescription: Categories, subcategories and tags, with a translation per locale.
taxonomy.title: Taxonomy
taxonomy.intro: Handles are permanent — they are in the public URL of every campaign filed under them, and the platform has no redirect table. Names and translations are what this screen edits.

users.metaDescription: Search the platform accounts, and stop the ones that have to be stopped.
users.title: Accounts
users.intro: Every account on the platform, searched by address, display name or profile slug. Suspending one signs it out everywhere and refuses it at sign-in; it changes nothing about the campaigns it created or the pledges it made, and those are separate decisions with separate consequences.

accountDetail.metaDescription: One account: its standing, the campaigns it created and the pledges it made.
accountDetail.title: Account
accountDetail.intro: One account, with everything a decision about it turns on: whether it is verified, whether it is suspended and why, what it has created, and what it has backed. Suspending is done from the directory, which is where the reason it asks for is recorded.

submissions.metaDescription: Campaigns their creators have submitted, waiting on a decision.
submissions.title: Campaigns for review
submissions.intro: Campaigns their creators have submitted, oldest first. Deciding one moves the campaign's own state: approving clears it for launch, requesting changes sends it back with a note, and rejecting is final.

campaigns.metaDescription: Every campaign on the platform, in any state, newest first.
campaigns.title: Campaigns
campaigns.intro: Every campaign on the platform, newest first, whatever state it is in. The review queue lists what is waiting on a decision; this lists everything, including drafts nobody has submitted and campaigns cleared for launch that have not launched.

campaignPreview.metaDescription: One campaign as its page reads, in any state, for the moderator deciding it.
campaignPreview.title: Campaign preview
campaignPreview.intro: The campaign as its public page would render it, whatever state it is in. The review queue links here because a campaign awaiting a decision has no public page — and a decision taken on a title and a goal figure is a guess.

legal.metaDescription: The eight documents §22.2 requires, their versions, and publishing them.
legal.title: Legal documents
legal.intro: A published version is never edited. A correction is a new version and the old one stays readable, because an acceptance names a version.

health.readFailed: The dashboard could not be read.

flags.subject: the feature flags
flags.heading: Flags
flags.emptyBody: Nothing on this deployment is behind a switch. Code asking for a flag that does not exist gets false, so the platform behaves as though every unbuilt feature is off — which is the safe direction.
flags.offForEverybody: off for everybody, including the accounts named on it
flags.addIntro: New flags arrive off and at nought percent. Widening a rollout only ever adds people — the accounts inside it are decided by a stable hash rather than a sample, so nobody loses a feature because the percentage went up.
flags.nameHint: Lower case and hyphenated, as the code asks for it.
flags.nameError: Lower case letters, digits and hyphens.

analytics.subject: the platform figures
analytics.otherCurrencyTitle: Some pledges are not in these totals
analytics.otherCurrencyBody: {count} pledges in the window were in another currency. §21.2 gives nothing to convert them with, so they are counted here and left out of the volume rather than added to a figure nobody could reconcile.
analytics.noneClosed: No campaign closed in this window. That is not a success rate of nought — it is the absence of one, which is why nothing is shown here.
analytics.nothingPledged: Nothing was pledged in this window.

notBuilt.FUNNELS: Funnels need the visit-to-pledge path; referral_touches records arrival, not what happened next (#313).

emailTemplates.readFailed: The templates could not be read.
emailTemplates.emptyBody: The platform sends no notifications on this deployment, which almost certainly means the message catalogue failed to load.

contentReports.noticeBody: Nothing could file a complaint about an update until this release, so this queue starts empty on every deployment and fills from here. Reports filed before it are about comments and campaigns, and they are on the other chips.

reportDetail.subject: this report
reportDetail.notFoundBody: That identifier does not name a report. It may have been decided and removed, or the link may be wrong.
reportDetail.decideFootnote: This records a judgement about the complaint and nothing else. Suspending the campaign, banning the account and removing the content are separate decisions with separate consequences, and none of them happens here.
reportDetail.historyIntro: Every privileged action recorded against this report, newest first — including the attempts that were refused. Read back from the audit trail rather than remembered by this screen, which is why it can answer for decisions taken last March.
reportDetail.historyFailedTitle: The history could not be read
reportDetail.historyEmpty: Nothing has been done to this report yet. A row appears here the moment somebody decides it.

evidence.subject: the reported content
evidence.heading: What was reported
evidence.intro: The content the complaint is about, read from the platform rather than from the complaint. A removed item is still shown, because a report filed before the removal still has to be decided.
evidence.failedTitle: The reported content could not be read
evidence.removedBody: Somebody has taken this down since the report was filed. It is shown here so that the complaint can still be decided — it does not need removing again.
evidence.goneTitle: This is no longer on the platform
evidence.goneBody: The identifier the report names no longer exists. It may have been purged, or its author's account anonymised. The complaint can still be decided; there is nothing left to read.
evidence.addressedBody: This report is about a campaign or an account rather than a piece of text. The console names it above and links to it — a fragment of a page beside a link to that page would be worse than the link alone.
evidence.noText: This item has no text of its own.

collections.subject: the collections
collections.heading: Collections
collections.emptyBody: A collection is a curated list with a public page of its own. Create one, add campaigns to it, then publish it.
collections.newIntro: Created unpublished and empty, so nothing is visible until it is worth seeing. The handle is half of its public URL and cannot be changed afterwards.
collections.titleHint: In Azerbaijani — the language the chain falls back to.
collections.createdNotice: {title} exists, unpublished and empty. Add campaigns, then publish it.
collections.publishedNotice: {title} is now visible to the public.
collections.unpublishedNotice: {title} has been taken down. The public gets a 404; the record stays.
collections.publishDescription: The list and its campaigns become visible to everybody.
collections.unpublishDescription: The public page starts answering 404. Nothing is deleted.
collections.publishBadgeBody: This collection grants the editorial badge, so publishing it badges every campaign in it.

collectionEditor.subject: this collection
collectionEditor.notFoundBody: That handle does not name a collection. Handles are permanent, so this is a wrong link rather than a rename.

hidden.one: One campaign here is not visible to the public — suspended, or no longer published. The membership row stays; the campaign stops being counted.
hidden.few: {count} campaigns here are not visible to the public — suspended, or no longer published. The membership row stays; the campaign stops being counted.
hidden.many: {count} campaigns here are not visible to the public — suspended, or no longer published. The membership row stays; the campaign stops being counted.
hidden.other: {count} campaigns here are not visible to the public — suspended, or no longer published. The membership row stays; the campaign stops being counted.

collectionEditor.addHint: Its identifier. It goes to the end of the list.
collectionEditor.emptyBody: A published collection with nothing in it is a page that says nothing. Add campaigns before publishing.
collectionEditor.addedNotice: The campaign is in the collection, at the end of it.
collectionEditor.removedNotice: {title} is out of the collection, and its badge with it.
collectionEditor.addDescription: It goes to the end of the list.
collectionEditor.removeDescription: It leaves the collection. Nothing about the campaign itself changes.
collectionEditor.addBadgeBody: This collection grants the editorial badge, so adding a campaign here is applying it.
collectionEditor.removeBadgeBody: This collection grants the editorial badge, so removing a campaign takes its badge with it.

badges.subject: the editorial badges
badges.heading: Collections that grant the badge
badges.emptyBody: No collection grants it, so no campaign shows one. Turn the grant on for a collection below, and every campaign in it is badged.
badges.restIntro: A staff selection is the usual carrier of the badge and does not imply it. The two are separate decisions, which is why they are separate columns and why this list exists.
badges.grantedNotice: {title} now grants the editorial badge to every campaign in it.
badges.grantDescription: Every campaign in this collection gains the editorial badge, including the ones already in it.
badges.stopDescription: Every campaign in this collection loses the editorial badge.
badges.dialogBody: This endpoint takes no note, so what you write here is not recorded — it is the pause before a change that affects every campaign in the list at once. The change itself is audited.

openCalls.subject: the open calls
openCalls.heading: Open calls
openCalls.emptyBody: An open call is a themed programme with a window it accepts entries in. Create one from the collections screen, choosing Open call as its kind — the kind cannot be guessed later.
openCalls.outsideWindow: Published, and outside its window — so the public page answers 404. That is the service's rule rather than a setting: a collection whose window has closed is not returned at all.
openCalls.opensHint: Empty means it has always been open.
openCalls.closesHint: Empty means it does not close.
openCalls.utcNote: Dates are read as midnight UTC. §21.2 gives the platform one convention and this follows it, so a programme closes at the same moment for everybody.

placements.subject: the placement
placements.heading: Placement order
placements.intro: Lower is earlier. This is the order of the collections index and of the rails built from it — one integer per collection, which is the whole of what placement means today.
placements.errorTitle: The order may not be what you asked for
placements.emptyBody: There are no collections yet. Create one on the collections screen, and it appears here.
placements.partial: A move is two requests; if the first succeeded, the order below is what the service now holds.

taxonomy.subject: the taxonomy
taxonomy.warningTitle: Handles are permanent and nothing here deletes
taxonomy.warningBody: A handle is in the public URL of every campaign filed under it, and the platform has no redirect table — so it cannot be changed after the entry is created. Nothing can be removed either: campaigns reference these rows, and retiring one needs a column the schema does not have yet.
taxonomy.emptyBody: No campaign can be filed anywhere until there is a category. Add one below.
taxonomy.tagsIntro: Read-only. §4.3 gives tags no editorial vocabulary — creators type them — so renaming one would be rewriting what somebody said about their own campaign. What this list is for is seeing which tags are heavy enough to become a category.
taxonomy.noTags: No creator has used a tag yet.

users.subject: the account directory
users.signedOutBody: This browser no longer has a session. Sign in again to read the account directory.
users.forbiddenBody: Accounts are searched and suspended by platform staff, and your account holds no platform role.
users.notStaff: Your account is not on the platform moderator list, so the account directory is not yours to read.
users.accountNotFound: That account no longer exists. It may have been deleted since this page was loaded.
users.selfSuspend: An account cannot suspend itself. Ask another moderator.
users.heading: Accounts
users.searchHint: An email address, a display name, or a profile slug.
users.filteredBody: Search matches an address, a display name or a profile slug, and it matches anywhere inside them.
users.emptyBody: Accounts appear here as people register.
users.suspendDescription: {email} will be signed out of every device and refused at sign-in until somebody reinstates them.
users.suspendBody: Their campaigns and pledges are left exactly where they are. This is reversible, unlike suspending a campaign — but every session they hold is revoked now and is not restored by reinstating them.
users.reasonHint: The person is told this, and an appeal is answered from it.
users.reasonRequired: Say why. The person is told this, and an appeal is answered from it.
users.reasonTooLong: A reason may not exceed {limit} characters.
users.suspendedNotice: {name} is suspended, and every session they held has been revoked.
users.reinstatedNotice: {name} can sign in again. Their old sessions are not restored.

accountDetail.subject: the account
accountDetail.campaignsFailed: This account's campaigns could not be read. Everything else on this page is what it says.
accountDetail.noCampaignsBody: This account has never created one, in any state — not even a draft.
accountDetail.pledgesFailed: This account's pledges could not be read. Everything else on this page is what it says.
accountDetail.noPledgesBody: This account has never backed a campaign.

support.subject: the support queue
support.heading: Open tickets
support.intro: Most urgent first, oldest first within a priority. Priority is set by staff — one the person asking could choose would be urgent on every ticket within a week.
support.emptyBody: No ticket is open or pending. Tickets are recorded here by staff when somebody writes in — there is no public form behind this screen yet.
support.filteredBody: Nothing matches these filters. Widen them, or go back to the queue.
support.assigneeHint: Whose tickets to show. Choosing somebody replaces "Nobody yet". Searching the directory is itself a recorded read.
support.ticketFailedTitle: The ticket could not be read
support.internalNote: internal note, never shown to them
support.internalLabel: Internal note — the requester never sees this, and it does not move the ticket

otherTickets.one: This account has asked us {count} other time
otherTickets.few: This account has asked us {count} other times
otherTickets.many: This account has asked us {count} other times
otherTickets.other: This account has asked us {count} other times

staff.subject: the staff roster
staff.notStaffBody: Your account holds no platform role, so the console has nothing to show you. This is not an error — the service refuses every screen behind this one, and the page you are on is simply saying so honestly.
staff.bootstrapBody: Your account is an administrator because its address is in {variable}, not because anybody granted it a role. That is the bootstrap the platform needs to make its first grant — once real roles are in place, empty that variable. Nobody can withdraw this from the console.
staff.rosterForbiddenBody: The roster names everybody who can move money on this platform, so reading it needs {capability} — which only an administrator holds. Your own standing is above, and it is the part that concerns you.
staff.rosterEmptyBody: Every member of staff on this deployment is an administrator through the bootstrap list. Grant real roles below and then empty that variable.
staff.grantIntro: Roles are additive: an account holds the union of every role granted to it. Nothing here takes a capability away, which is why there is no order to resolve.

capability.MODERATE_CONTENT: Work the moderation and report queues
capability.ADMINISTER_ACCOUNTS: Search, inspect, ban and reinstate accounts
capability.CURATE: Edit collections, badges, placement and the taxonomy
capability.VIEW_FINANCE: Read the payment log, the ledger and the platform figures
capability.APPROVE_PAYOUT: Sign off and send a payout
capability.CONFIGURE_PLATFORM: Change fees, feature flags and email copy
capability.VIEW_HEALTH: Read queue depth and provider status
capability.PUBLISH_LEGAL_DOCUMENT: Publish a version of a legal document
capability.READ_ACCEPTANCE_RECORD: Read what an account has agreed to, and when
capability.READ_SIGNED_AGREEMENT: Read an account's signed creator agreement, with the name and FİN on the certificate
capability.REVIEW_IDENTITY_VERIFICATION: Approve or reject an identity verification
capability.OPEN_IDENTITY_DOCUMENT: Open an identity document — the most sensitive read on the platform
capability.VERIFY_PAYOUT_DESTINATION: Confirm that a payout destination belongs to its creator
capability.GRANT_COMPLIANCE_OVERRIDE: Waive a compliance requirement for one account, for a bounded time

picker.subject: the account directory
picker.label: Account
picker.hint: Search by name, email address or profile path. Every search of the directory is recorded, so it runs when you ask for it.
picker.failedTitle: The directory could not be searched

staff.chooseAccountFirst: Choose an account before granting a role.

payments.subject: the payment log
payments.heading: Provider calls
payments.identifierHint: A campaign or a pledge. The whole identifier, not part of one.
payments.emptyBody: Every call to a payment provider is recorded here, including the ones that were refused. An empty log means no collection has run on this deployment.
payments.filteredBody: Nothing matches that identifier and that outcome. Check the identifier, which of the two it is, and whether the outcome is the one you meant.
payments.noReference: The provider gave no reference. This attempt may have reached it.

ledger.subject: the ledger
ledger.heading: Postings

unbalanced.one: One posting on this page has debits that do not equal their credits. The database refuses to commit that, so these rows did not arrive through the application. Raise it before doing anything else.
unbalanced.few: {count} postings on this page have debits that do not equal their credits. The database refuses to commit that, so these rows did not arrive through the application. Raise it before doing anything else.
unbalanced.many: {count} postings on this page have debits that do not equal their credits. The database refuses to commit that, so these rows did not arrive through the application. Raise it before doing anything else.
unbalanced.other: {count} postings on this page have debits that do not equal their credits. The database refuses to commit that, so these rows did not arrive through the application. Raise it before doing anything else.

ledger.campaignHint: A campaign identifier, to see only what moved on it.
ledger.emptyBody: A posting is written when money actually moves. An empty ledger means no collection has succeeded on this deployment.
ledger.filteredBody: No posting has touched that account on that campaign. Widen the filters, or check the identifier.
ledger.balancesNote: Debits minus credits, per currency and never summed across them. Not narrowed by the account filter above.

reconciliation.subject: the reconciliation
reconciliation.readFailed: The reconciliation could not be read.
reconciliation.runForbidden: Your session no longer has permission to run a reconciliation.
reconciliation.neverRunTitle: Nothing has been reconciled on this replica
reconciliation.neverRunBody: The nightly pass keeps its result in the process that made it, so a replica that has restarted since 02:30 has nothing to report — which is not the same as balanced books. Run one now to get an answer.
reconciliation.unbalancedNote: {emphasis} — the entry that would fix this depends on which of a dozen things went wrong, so it is a decision rather than a sweep.
reconciliation.nothingHeld: The platform holds no money in any account yet, which is balanced rather than unchecked.

finding.LEDGER_NOT_ZERO: The ledger does not sum to zero in {currency}: net {amount}.
finding.CREATOR_OVERPAID: {account} is positive at {amount}, which is a creator paid more than they earned.
finding.PLATFORM_ACCOUNT_NEGATIVE: {account} is negative at {amount}, which is money disbursed that was never taken.
finding.DISAGREES_WITH_PAYMENTS: The ledger holds {amount} and the transactions say {other}.

reconciliation.runNote: Two queries over the whole platform. It reads and writes nothing, so running it is safe at any time — and it is the only way to get an answer from the replica you are talking to.

findingTitle.UNBALANCED: The ledger does not sum to zero
findingTitle.IMPOSSIBLE_SIGN: An account holds a balance it cannot hold
findingTitle.DISAGREES_WITH_PAYMENTS: The ledger and the payment records disagree

findingMeaning.UNBALANCED: PostgreSQL refuses a posting whose debits and credits differ, so a row got past both the application and that trigger. Nothing else on this platform can produce it.
findingMeaning.IMPOSSIBLE_SIGN: Escrow below zero is money paid out that was never taken; a creator’s account above zero is a creator paid more than they earned. Neither is caught by the sum, because two errors of opposite sign balance perfectly.
findingMeaning.DISAGREES_WITH_PAYMENTS: What the ledger holds and what the transactions say moved are not the same figure. This is the only check that catches a posting the application never made at all.

payouts.subject: the payout queue
payouts.calculateHeading: Work out what a campaign owes
payouts.calculateIntro: The figures are frozen at this moment and never recomputed — a payout two people approved has to be the payout that is sent. If the collections or refunds move afterwards, the send is refused and a fresh calculation replaces it.
payouts.calculatedNotice: Calculated {amount} for {id}. The hold runs until {date}.
payouts.emptyTitle: Nothing is waiting to be paid
payouts.emptyBody: No campaign has a payout in flight. Work one out above once a campaign has closed and collected.
payouts.payoutFailedTitle: The payout could not be read
payouts.noSignatures: Nobody has signed this off yet.
payouts.needsTwo: It is above the threshold, so it needs two different people.
payouts.stillHeldBody: §9's hold runs until {date}. It exists so that refunds and chargebacks land before the money leaves, so a signature given now would be a signature on a figure nobody can yet know is right.
payouts.youHaveSigned: You have already signed this payout. A second signature has to be somebody else.
payouts.awaitingHold: Cannot be signed until the hold expires on {date}.
payouts.destinationHeldTitle: This creator's payout destination is not confirmed
payouts.destinationHeldBody: This payout is {standing}. Money goes only to an account the creator supplied and a compliance reviewer confirmed — never to one typed here.

destinationStanding.NONE: waiting — the creator has not said where they are paid
destinationStanding.AWAITING_VERIFICATION: waiting on a compliance reviewer to confirm the account
destinationStanding.NAME_MISMATCH: waiting — the account is held by a differently named party
destinationStanding.REJECTED: waiting — the account was refused and the creator has to file another

payouts.verificationHeldTitle: The creator's identity has not been verified
payouts.verificationHeldBody: This payout is {standing}. Money leaves only to somebody the platform has identified; the creator has already been asked for what is missing.

standing.NEVER_REQUESTED: waiting — nothing had been asked of the creator, and it has been asked now
standing.AWAITING_DOCUMENTS: waiting for the creator to send documents
standing.REJECTED: waiting — the documents were refused and the creator has to send others
standing.EXPIRED: waiting — the approval has aged out and the creator has to verify again

refunds.subject: the refund log
refunds.issueIntro: Leave the amount blank to refund whatever is left on the pledge. The reason code is what refunds are counted by; the note is what the next person reads.
refunds.noteHint: Required. A code is never the whole story.
refunds.emptyBody: No money has gone back on this deployment. Every refund the platform issues is recorded here, including the ones a provider refused.
refunds.filteredBody: Nothing is in that state. A refund that stays REQUESTED is one worth chasing; the others are settled.

reason.DISPUTE_CONCEDED: A chargeback we did not contest

disputes.subject: the chargeback queue
disputes.noticeTitle: Evidence is sent through the provider
disputes.noticeBody: Submitting here records that the case was answered and by whom. §9.3's provider interface has no evidence upload, so the documents themselves still go through the provider's own console — this screen is the platform's record of the case, not the channel to the network.
disputes.heading: Open cases
disputes.emptyBody: Nothing is waiting for an answer. Cases arrive here from a provider webhook, so an empty queue means no network has disputed a charge.

reason.bank_cannot_process: The bank could not process it

disputes.caseFailedTitle: The case could not be read
disputes.noEvidence: Nothing has been assembled. A case answered with no evidence is a case conceded slowly.
disputes.outcomeNote: Recording LOST or CONCEDED posts the disputed amount and the provider's fee to the ledger. WON posts nothing, because nothing moved.

evidenceKind.RECEIPT: What they were charged, and for what
evidenceKind.REFUND_POLICY: What our refund policy said at the time
evidenceKind.ACTIVITY_LOG: That the cardholder was the one who pledged

fees.subject: the fee schedule
fees.noticeTitle: Changing a fee opens a new schedule
fees.noticeBody: There is no edit. Submitting below closes the terms currently in force and opens new ones beginning now, so a payout calculated last month still prices against last month's rates. Nothing you can do here changes what was charged in the past.
fees.emptyBody: The platform is currently pricing every payout at zero fees. That is deliberate — a payout run must not stop because nobody wrote a row — but it means creators are being paid the full amount collected.
fees.whyHint: Required. A fee change nobody explained is one nobody can defend.
fees.openedNotice: New {scope} terms in force from {date}. The previous schedule is closed, not deleted.
fees.pastIntro: What the platform charged, and when. §22.1 makes this a record with a retention rule rather than a changelog.

plans.subject: the plan catalogue
plans.noticeTitle: Editing a plan reaches its subscribers
plans.noticeBody: A price change applies to new purchases only: what somebody was charged is written on their own subscription. A limit change applies to everybody on the plan, at their next submission rather than retroactively. There is no delete — take a plan off sale instead.
plans.catalogueIntro: Retired plans are listed too, because their subscribers still hold them.
plans.emptyCatalogueBody: Publishing is gated on a plan, so with an empty catalogue nobody can send a campaign for review. Add one below.
plans.planSummary: {price} {period} · {campaigns} campaigns at a time · goals up to {ceiling}
plans.codeHint: Upper case, no spaces. It cannot be changed afterwards.
plans.descriptionHint: One line under the name on the pricing page.
plans.priceHint: In AZN. Zero means a free tier.
plans.queueIntro: No payment provider is integrated yet, so a paid plan starts when somebody here records that the transfer arrived. Every activation is audited under your name.
plans.emptyQueueBody: No subscription is waiting for a payment to be recorded against it.
plans.noteHint: The transfer reference or invoice number, so this can be checked later.
plans.endReasonHint: Required. This takes the plan away at once rather than at the period end.
plans.addedNotice: {plan} was added and is on sale.
plans.repricedNotice: {plan} was repriced. Existing subscribers keep what they were charged.

submissionQueue.signedOutTitle: Sign in to work the queue
submissionQueue.signedOutBody: This screen reads campaigns awaiting a decision, which needs a signed-in member of staff.
submissionQueue.forbiddenBody: Reviewing campaigns needs the content moderation capability. Ask an administrator if you should have it.
submissionQueue.notStaff: Reviewing campaigns is done by platform staff.
submissionQueue.transitionNotAllowed: The campaign is no longer in a state this decision can be taken from. Reload the queue.
submissionQueue.transitionNotAllowedFrom: Somebody has already decided this one — it is now {state}.
submissionQueue.unreachable: We could not reach the service. Try again.

emptyBody.SUBMITTED: Every campaign submitted so far has been decided.
emptyBody.CHANGES_REQUESTED: No campaign is currently with its creator awaiting changes.
emptyBody.APPROVED: Approved campaigns appear here until they launch.
emptyBody.REJECTED: Refused campaigns stay here so the decision can be read back.

campaignDirectory.subject: the campaign directory
campaignDirectory.heading: Campaigns
campaignDirectory.searchHint: A title, a creator, a path, or a whole identifier.
campaignDirectory.emptyBody: A campaign appears here the moment somebody starts one, long before it is submitted for review.
campaignDirectory.filteredBody: Nothing matches this search and this state. Choose another state, or shorten the search.

campaignPreview.subject: this campaign
campaignPreview.notFoundBody: That identifier does not name a campaign, or its creator is inside the deletion grace period and the page has nobody to attribute it to.
campaignPreview.previewNoticeBody: The campaign as its public page would render it, in whatever state it is in — including a draft, which its creator has shown nobody. Nothing on this screen changes anything: approving, rejecting and suspending are elsewhere, and closing this tab loses none of them.
campaignPreview.notPublicYet: This campaign has no public page in its current state.
campaignPreview.noStory: The creator has not written one yet. Submission requires it, so a campaign awaiting review will have it.
campaignPreview.noRisks: Nothing written yet. Submission requires two hundred characters of it.

legal.subject: the legal documents
legal.noticeBody: A published version is never edited and never deleted. A correction is a new version; the old one stays readable, because somebody who accepted it is entitled to read what they accepted.
legal.languageHint: The Azerbaijani text is the one that governs. The other three exist so a person can read what they are agreeing to.
legal.draftIntro: One draft per language. Saving again replaces the open draft rather than starting a second one.
legal.bodyHint: The text itself is stored, not a link to it. The acceptance record has to reproduce this text years from now.
legal.savedNotice: Saved the draft of version {version} in {locale}.
legal.publishIntro: Every open draft is published together, under one version number and one effective date.
legal.governingMissingBody: The Azerbaijani version is the one that governs, so nothing publishes without it.
legal.effectiveFromHint: Leave empty for now. A future date is allowed; a past one is refused.
legal.nothingDraftedBody: Write the text above first. Publishing twice does nothing the second time.
legal.historyIntro: Every version stays readable: somebody who accepted one is entitled to read what they accepted.
legal.noVersionsBody: This document has no text yet, so nothing on the platform requires it.

decidedBy.OPEN: Open, and decided by moderator {moderator} on {at}.

decision.noteRequired: Say why. The creator is shown this note and has to act on it.
decision.tooLong: A note may not exceed {limit} characters.

uphold.title: Uphold this report?
uphold.description: The complaint about {name} is recorded as justified. This cannot be undone.
uphold.body: Nothing is taken down by this. Suspending a campaign or banning an account are separate decisions, and this one does not make them for you.
uphold.noteHint: Optional. Written for the next moderator, not for the person who reported this — nothing shows it to them.

dismiss.title: Dismiss this report?
dismiss.description: The complaint about {name} is recorded as unjustified. This cannot be undone.
dismiss.body: Dismissals are audited too. “Who dismissed the fourteen reports about this campaign” is the question an investigation starts from.
dismiss.noteHint: Optional. Written for the next moderator, not for the person who reported this — nothing shows it to them.

decision.campaignBody: This moves the campaign. It does not decide the report — that is still open, and still yours to uphold or dismiss.

request-changes.title: Send this campaign back?
request-changes.description: {name} goes back to its creator, who can fix it and submit again.
request-changes.noteHint: Required. The creator is shown this and has to act on it — it is the entire content of the state.

reject.title: Reject this campaign?
reject.description: {name} is refused. Rejection is TERMINAL — there is no way back to a draft.
reject.noteHint: Required. The creator is shown this. If the problem is fixable, send the campaign back instead.

language.title: Language and currency
language.intro: How IdeaNest writes to you, and the currency you read amounts in.
language.fieldHint: Applies to your account pages straight away. The public site is still in English while the rest of the translation is written.
language.failed: That language could not be saved. Try again.

currency.title: Currency
currency.intro: Choose the currency amounts are shown to you in. Campaigns are still funded in manat.
currency.fieldHint: An approximation, converted from the Central Bank of Azerbaijan’s daily rate. Every campaign is funded in manat and your card is charged in manat.
currency.failed: That currency could not be saved. Reload the page and try again.
currency.unavailable: Amounts are shown in Azerbaijani manat. There is no other currency to choose from right now — a display currency needs a published exchange rate, and the platform has none it can use today.

profile.metaDescription: Your name, biography, picture, website, location and links, as everybody else sees them.
profile.title: Profile
profile.intro: What strangers see when they open your profile or a campaign you created. To hide the page altogether, go to <privacy>privacy</privacy>.

notifications.metaDescription: Choose what IdeaNest tells you, and how it reaches you.
notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.intro: Choose what you are told and how it reaches you. As it happens sends each one on its own; daily digest collects them into one message a day, where the channel supports it. In app is what fills your notifications. Changes save as you make them.

sessions.metaDescription: Review the devices signed in to your IdeaNest account and sign out of any of them.
sessions.title: Devices
sessions.intro: Every device currently signed in to your account. If you do not recognise one, sign it out — it stops being able to refresh within fifteen minutes.

email.metaDescription: Move your IdeaNest account to a different email address.
email.title: Email address
email.intro: The address you sign in with, and where everything IdeaNest sends you goes. To change your password instead, go to <password>password</password>.

password.metaDescription: Change the password on your IdeaNest account.
password.title: Password
password.intro: Changing it needs the one you have now. If you do not have it — or you have only ever signed in with Google or Apple — <reset>reset it by email</reset> instead.

security.metaDescription: Add a code from your phone to your IdeaNest sign-in.
security.title: Two-factor authentication
security.intro: A code from your phone, on top of your password. §4.1 requires it before a payout, so a creator will meet it sooner or later. To see which browsers are signed in, go to <devices>devices</devices>.

privacy.metaDescription: Choose who can see your profile, download a copy of your IdeaNest data, or close your account.
privacy.title: Privacy, data and closure
privacy.intro: Who can see you, everything IdeaNest holds about you, and what happens to it if you leave.

emailChange.heading: Change your email address
emailChange.signInWithUnverified: You sign in with {address}, which is not verified yet.
emailChange.alertTitle: The account moves when the new address answers
emailChange.alertBody: We send a link to the address you give us and a notice to the one you have now. Your account keeps its current address until that link is opened, so a typo costs you nothing but the message.
emailChange.currentPasswordHint: Asked for so that a stolen sign-in cannot move the address that resets your password.
emailChange.sentIntro: A confirmation link is on its way to {address}. Opening it is what moves the account.
emailChange.stillSignIn: You still sign in with {address} until that link is opened, and it works for six hours.
emailChange.stillSignInUnknown: Your current address still signs in until that link is opened, and it works for six hours.

about.metaDescription: What IdeaNest is, how all-or-nothing funding works, and what it costs.
about.title: About IdeaNest
about.summary: A place to fund things that do not exist yet, on terms that are the same for everybody.
about.intro: IdeaNest is a reward-based crowdfunding platform. A creator publishes a campaign with a goal and a deadline; people who want the thing to exist pledge towards it; and if the goal is met by the deadline, the pledges are collected and the creator makes the thing. If it is not, nobody is charged at all.

allOrNothing.heading: All or nothing, and why it is not a detail
allOrNothing.first: A partly funded campaign is worse than an unfunded one. It leaves a creator holding money that is not enough to finish with and backers holding a promise nobody can keep. So a campaign that misses its goal collects nothing, costs its creator no fee, and leaves every card untouched.
allOrNothing.second: The consequence is that a deadline means something. A campaign at 90% on its last day is genuinely at risk, and the platform says so rather than dressing it up.

cost.heading: What it costs
cost.successful: A successful campaign pays 5% of what it raised, plus the payment processor’s own fee — roughly 2.5–3% and a small fixed amount per pledge.
cost.unsuccessful: An unsuccessful campaign pays nothing. No listing fee, no platform fee, no processing fee.
cost.note: Rates are configuration rather than code, so a category or an individual agreement can carry a different one. The rate above is the standard schedule.

notAPurchase.heading: A pledge is not a purchase
notAPurchase.body: This is the sentence most worth reading twice. Backing a campaign funds an attempt. The creator is accountable for the attempt and for telling backers honestly how it is going; they are not a shop with the thing in a warehouse. Every campaign has to publish its risks and challenges before it can be submitted, and that section is required rather than encouraged.

howItWorks.metaDescription: Backing a campaign, running one, and what happens between a pledge and a parcel on IdeaNest.
howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.summary: What happens between finding a campaign and holding the thing it funded.

backing.heading: If you are backing something
backing.first: Choose a reward tier, or pledge without one. Your card is authorised and nothing is taken while the campaign is running — you can change your pledge, move to a different tier, add an extra, or cancel outright until the deadline.
backing.second: At the deadline one of two things happens. If the campaign reached its goal, every confirmed pledge is collected and the campaign moves into fulfilment. If it did not, nothing is collected, no fee is charged, and the stored card tokens are deleted within thirty days.
backing.third: A card can fail at collection — expired, out of funds, refused by a bank. There is a seven-day window in which it is retried before the pledge is given up on.

surveys.heading: Then the creator asks you some questions
surveys.first: Most rewards need something the campaign page cannot know: a size, a colour, an edition, and somewhere to send it. That arrives as a survey, and it appears under <surveys>surveys</surveys> in your account. Your shipping address is held separately from your answers and encrypted at rest, and it belongs to the pledge rather than to your account — so two campaigns can go to two different places.
surveys.second: As parcels go out, <deliveries>deliveries</deliveries> shows the carrier and the tracking number for each one.

running.heading: If you are running a campaign
running.draft: Draft it. A title, a summary, a category, a goal, a duration between one and sixty days, and a cover image. The story needs at least 500 characters and the risks section at least 200 — both are required.
running.rewards: Add rewards. Up to a hundred tiers, each with a price, what is in it, and where it ships. A tier’s price cannot change once the campaign is live, and a tier with backers cannot be deleted — only hidden.
running.submit: Submit it for review. A person reads it. They approve it, ask for changes, or reject it with a reason.
running.launch: Launch. From this point the goal and the deadline are fixed. Everything else — the story, the updates, the reward quantities upwards — stays editable.
running.deliver: Deliver. Send the survey, collect the addresses, lock them when you start printing labels, and record tracking as parcels go out.

agreeing.heading: What you are agreeing to as a backer
agreeing.first: A pledge funds an attempt rather than buying a finished object. The creator owes you an honest account of how it is going — that is what campaign updates are for — and the platform owes you the tools to see it and to report a campaign that is not being honest. Neither of those is the same as a guarantee that the thing will arrive.
agreeing.second: <trustSafety>Trust and safety</trustSafety> sets out what is checked, and what to do when something is wrong.

trustSafety.metaDescription: How campaigns are reviewed, what is not allowed, how to report something, and what happens to your money and your data.
trustSafety.title: Trust and safety
trustSafety.summary: What is checked, what is not, and what to do when something looks wrong.

review.heading: Every campaign is read before it goes live
review.first: A campaign cannot publish itself. It is submitted, a person reviews it against the rules below, and it is approved, sent back for changes, or rejected with a reason. Nothing on the platform reaches the public without passing through that.
review.second: Review is not verification. A reviewer checks that a campaign is what it says it is, is allowed to be funded, and is not somebody else’s work. They are not in a position to confirm that a creator can manufacture what they have drawn — which is why a pledge is described everywhere on this platform as funding an attempt.

notAllowed.heading: What is not allowed
notAllowed.prohibited: Prohibited items — things the platform does not allow to be funded at all.
notAllowed.misrepresentation: Misrepresentation — a campaign that states something untrue about itself.
notAllowed.notOwn: Work that is not the creator’s own, or that uses somebody else’s intellectual property.
notAllowed.offensive: Offensive material, and content that targets people for who they are.
notAllowed.spam: Spam, and campaigns that exist to advertise something else.
notAllowed.fraud: Fraud — where there is reason to believe nobody intends to deliver.

reporting.heading: Reporting something
reporting.first: A campaign, a comment or an account can be reported by anybody with an IdeaNest account. A report goes to a moderator, not to an automatic filter: nothing disappears because five people objected to it, and a report is a request for a person to look.
reporting.second: Reporting the same thing twice does not add weight — the second report returns the first one. Reports are not public, and the account being reported is not told who reported it.

money.heading: Your money
money.first: Card details never reach IdeaNest’s own servers; payments go through the provider’s hosted fields. While a campaign is running your pledge is an authorisation rather than a charge, and a campaign that misses its goal takes nothing at all.
money.second: Every payment operation is idempotent, which is the unglamorous property that matters most: a request that is retried because a connection dropped produces one pledge and one charge, not two.

account.heading: Your account and your data
account.twoFactor: Two-factor authentication is available on every account and required before a payout. Set it up under two-factor authentication.
account.devices: Every signed-in device is listed under devices, and any of them can be signed out from any other.
account.addresses: Shipping addresses are encrypted at rest and are visible to a creator only for the campaign you backed.
account.data: A copy of your data is a download, and closing your account keeps it for thirty days before anonymising it — so a closure made in anger, or by somebody else, can be undone. Both are under data and closure.

limits.heading: What we cannot do
limits.first: IdeaNest cannot make a campaign deliver. What it can do is keep the record honest: a campaign’s updates, its comments and the way to report it are all on the campaign’s own page, where somebody deciding whether to back it will see them.
limits.second: A creator can moderate comments on their own campaign, and a removed one does not vanish — the row stays, marked as removed. A comment thread that has been cleaned out therefore still looks like one, which is the point: a page with nothing on it and a page with twelve removals are different things, and a reader is entitled to tell them apart.
